'''''Hakea sericea''''', commonly known as '''bushy needlewood''' or '''silky hakea''',<ref name="ANBG">{{cite web |title=''Hakea sericea'' |url=https://www.anbg.gov.au/common.names/ |website=Integrated Botanical Information System |publisher=Australian National Botanic Garden |access-date=9 September 2019}}</ref> is a shrub with a profusion of mainly white flowers from July for several months. It is [[endemism|endemic]] to eastern Australia. It has become an environmental weed in some countries.

==Description==
''Hakea sericea'' is a large spreading, bushy shrub and may grow to {{convert|4|m|ft|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} and does not form a [[lignotuber]]. The branchlets are densely covered in grey-whitish short, soft, woolly hairs.  The [[inflorescence]] appear in [[umbel]]s  of 1–6 flowers in leaf axils, pinkish in bud and maturing to white. The inflorescence [[rachis]] is {{cvt|0.5–2.5|mm}} long and thickly covered in woolly, short, matted white hairs toward the end and rusty coloured at the base. The [[pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]s are {{cvt|2–4|mm}} long, slight to densely covered with long white hairs. The smooth [[perianth]] is {{cvt|2.5–4.7|mm}} long and the [[pistil]] {{cvt|4–7.5|mm}} long. The needle-shaped leaves are grooved on the undersurface and up to {{convert|7|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|0.7-1.3|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide and ending in a sharp point {{cvt|1–2|mm}} long. The leaves are moderately covered with flattened silky hairs, quickly becoming smooth. 
The fruit are rough and coarsely wrinkled with a network of veins on the surface, {{convert|2.5-3|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide ending with a short, broad beak to {{cvt|3|mm}} long.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Hakea~sericea|title=Hakea sericea Schrad. & J.C.Wendl.|work=New South Wales flora online|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens & Domain Trust, Sydney Australia|access-date=8 August 2008}}</ref><ref name="DUI">{{cite book |last1=Holliday |first1=Ivan |title=Hakeas:A Field and Garden Guide |publisher=Reed New Holland |isbn=1-877069-14-0}}</ref><ref name="FAIRLE">{{cite book |last1=Fairley |first1=Alan |last2=Moore |first2=Philip |title=Native Plants of the Sydney Region |publisher=Jacana Books-Allen and Unwin |isbn=978-1-74175-571-8}}</ref><ref name="SAF">{{cite web |title=''Hakea sericea'' |url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/efsa/lucid/Hakea/key/Australian%20Hakea%20species/Media/Html/Hakea_sericea.htm |website=eFlora South Australia |publisher=Govt. of South Australia |access-date=9 September 2019}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Hakea sericea'' was first formally described by [[Heinrich Schrader (botanist)|Heinrich Schrader]] and [[Johann Christoph Wendland]] in 1797 and published the description in ''Sertum Hannoveranum''.<ref name="APNI">{{cite web |title=''Hakea sericea'' |url=https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/526202 |website=APNI |access-date=16 November 2018}}</ref>  The genus ''Hakea'' is named after [[Baron Christian Ludwig von Hake (botanist, born 1745)|Baron von Hake]], patron of botany in the 18th century. ''Sericea'' meaning silky, referring to the tiny hairs on young growth.<ref name="SAF"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
Silky hakea is found from the coast and adjacent ranges of south-eastern Queensland to south-eastern New South Wales. A frost tolerant species, grows in well-drained soil and full sun. A good habitat plant due to its prickly habit and winter flowering. It is also naturalised in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] and possibly South Australia.<ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |title=''Hakea sericea'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/58679623-1c49-4934-b842-7652d21605f0 |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |access-date=22 June 2020}}</ref>

''H. sericea'' is an invasive weed in some areas outside Australia, specifically in [[South Africa]], [[New Zealand]] and [[Portugal]].<ref name=nz>[https://www.weedbusters.org.nz/weed-information/weed-list/needlebush/ Weedbusters NZ:  Needlebush.] Retrieved 8 December 2018.</ref><ref name="GNP">{{cite web |title=''Hakea sericea'' |url=https://www.anbg.gov.au/gnp/gnp3/hakea-sericea.html |website=Growing Native Plants |publisher=Australian National Botanic Gardens |access-date=9 September 2019}}</ref>

In the [[European Union]], due to the significant negative impacts of its introduction to the ecosystem, it is included in the [[list of invasive alien species of Union concern]] and hence cannot be imported, bred, transported, commercialized, or intentionally released into the environment in any of its member states.<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of Invasive Alien Species of Union concern |url=https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02016R1141-20250807 |date=7 August 2025 |access-date=8 May 2026|website=eur-lex.europa.eu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Regulation No. 1143/2014 of the European parliament and of the council of 22 October 2014 on the prevention and management of the introduction and spread of invasive alien species |url=https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32014R1143&from=EN |publisher=European Union |date=2014-11-04 |location=Strasbourg |access-date=2026-05-08 |archive-date=2017-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303185733/http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32014R1143&from=EN |url-status=live }}</ref>
